policies.title: Big Cat Public Safety Act
policies.summary: Restricted private possession, breeding and public contact with covered big cats.
policies.changed: Added federal possession and breeding restrictions alongside commerce rules.
policies.afterward: FWS implemented regulations in June 2023; grandfather registration closed June 18.
policies.attribution: Congress enacted the law, Biden signed it, and FWS administered it.
policies.unknown: No verified national before/after welfare or population series was located in this review.
policies.mechanism: Reduce new private ownership and direct public-contact exploitation.
policies.coverage: Lions, tigers, leopards, snow/clouded leopards, jaguars, cheetahs, cougars and hybrids.
policies.exceptions: Qualifying exhibitors, sanctuaries, state institutions/veterinarians, transporters and registered pre-Act owners; conditions apply.
policies.confidenceReason: Statute and implementation verified; effect estimates were not located in this review.

policies.title: Shark finning and fin sales restrictions
policies.status: Sales prohibition in force; limited exemptions
policies.summary: The 2022 fin-sales law builds on national finning restrictions and attached-fin landing rules.
policies.changed: Prohibited covered detached-fin possession and trade.
policies.afterward: NOAA reported zero declared fin exports in 2023; reported fin imports had ceased before the December 2022 sales ban. The 2019 import value is disputed across NOAA records.
policies.attribution: Congress enacted successive laws; agency rules and state bans also contributed. Biden signed the 2022 measure.
policies.unknown: Illegal trade, displacement and causal changes in shark deaths or suffering are unmeasured here.
policies.mechanism: Reduce market access and strengthen enforcement; conservation and individual welfare are separate endpoints.
policies.coverage: U.S. possession, transport and trade in shark fins.
policies.exceptions: Specified noncommercial scientific/subsistence purposes and smooth/spiny dogfish; lawful whole sharks with fins attached may still be traded.
policies.confidenceReason: Declared trade result verified, causal attribution unresolved.

contributors.role: Rules, enforcement and prior state restrictions

history.event: Shark Conservation Act added attached-fin requirements.
NOAA recorded zero declared fin exports.

policies.title: FDA Modernization Act 2.0 and FDA alternatives implementation
policies.status: 2022 law operative; guidance drafts and 2026 direct final rule not yet effective
policies.summary: Expanded acceptable nonclinical methods; FDA later developed a roadmap and guidance for alternatives.
policies.changed: Nonclinical testing definition explicitly includes cell assays, organ chips, computation and animal tests.
policies.afterward: FDA reported 2026 milestones; September 2026 terminology direct final rule is scheduled for February 2027 subject to the adverse-comment process.
policies.attribution: Congress/Biden supplied the 2022 statutory change; Trump II FDA led the 2025–26 implementation.
policies.unknown: No verified count of experiments replaced or animals spared attributable to these measures was located in this review.
policies.mechanism: Permit scientifically suitable alternatives and reduce routine testing.
policies.coverage: FDA-regulated drug nonclinical evidence; specific guidance has narrower scope.
policies.exceptions: Animal evidence remains permissible; this is no universal animal-testing ban.
policies.confidenceReason: Legal option and documents verified; projected outcomes remain uncertain.

history.event: Section 3209 of Public Law 117-328 amended nonclinical testing provisions.

history.status: direct final rule, future effective date
history.event: Terminology rule and companion proposal published; scheduled effective February 4, 2027 subject to withdrawal.

policies.title: NIH Complement-ARIE and human-based research initiatives
policies.status: Program, funding and office implementation; continued animal-model eligibility
policies.summary: NIH developed alternatives infrastructure and broadened funding opportunities.
policies.changed: Complement-ARIE began in 2024; July 2025 funding notices must also support human-focused approaches.
policies.afterward: NIH announced more than $150 million in first awards in March 2026 and established ORIVA in June.
policies.attribution: Biden-era program development preceded Trump II funding and organizational implementation.
policies.unknown: Net animal-use reduction, substitution, total expenditures and validated welfare outcomes.
policies.mechanism: Develop and validate alternative methods and broaden applicant choice.
policies.coverage: NIH research opportunities and methods infrastructure.
policies.exceptions: NIH clarified that scientifically appropriate animal-only proposals remain eligible.
policies.confidenceReason: Dates and policy scope verified; no outcome evaluation was located in this review.

history.event: New animal-model NOFOs must also support human-focused approaches.
Animal-only applications remain eligible where justified.

policies.title: Federal chimpanzee retirement and noninvasive-only research policy
policies.status: Retirement framework implemented; permitted noninvasive research continues
policies.summary: Federal sanctuary legislation developed into NIH's termination of support for invasive chimpanzee research.
policies.changed: NIH retired its reserve research colony in 2015; 2016 rules limited future support to permissible noninvasive work.
policies.afterward: Transfers extended across administrations; litigation challenged refusal to transfer Alamogordo chimpanzees; sanctuary reports their arrival in 2025.
policies.attribution: Congress/Clinton created the framework; sanctuary operation began under Bush; Obama-era NIH ended invasive support; later administrations, courts and Chimp Haven handled transfers.
policies.unknown: No nationwide causal estimate of health or suffering improvement from the 2015 policy was located in this review.
policies.mechanism: End invasive research and provide lifetime care.
policies.exceptions: Qualifying noninvasive behavioral and veterinary-record research; other primates remain outside this chimpanzee-specific change.
policies.confidenceReason: Policy, GAO audit and court intervention verified; welfare study is narrower.

history.event: NIH ended reserve colony and made remaining NIH-owned chimpanzees retirement-eligible.
GAO snapshot distinguished eligibility from completed relocation.
Chimp Haven reports arrival of all remaining Alamogordo chimpanzees.
NIH changed review administration while retaining 2016 criteria.

policies.title: AWA research exclusions and incomplete national animal-use counting
policies.status: Statutory exclusions remain; NIH annual-count proposal under consultation
policies.summary: AWA research counts omit purpose-bred Mus mice, Rattus rats and birds, among other excluded animals.
policies.changed: The 2002 statute codified exclusions; current APHIS summaries count the covered population.
policies.afterward: NIH in October 2026 sought comment on broader annual vertebrate reporting.
policies.attribution: Congress/Bush enacted the exclusion; APHIS administers reports; Trump II NIH proposed broader transparency.
policies.unknown: Complete comparable national annual research-animal totals and aggregate suffering.
policies.mechanism: Defines regulatory coverage and visibility; reporting is not itself welfare improvement.
policies.coverage: APHIS-covered warm-blooded animals, subject to statutory exclusions.
policies.exceptions: Purpose-bred research mice/rats/birds, cold-blooded animals and food/fiber agricultural uses are outside these APHIS totals; other oversight may apply.
policies.confidenceReason: Legal scope and reporting distinction documented.

contributors.role: Separate PHS oversight and proposed reporting

history.event: NIH describes annual-number reporting proposal; current annual OLAW reports do not require counts.

policies.title: AWA welfare standards for regulated birds
policies.status: Compliance phases completed; current APHIS guidance verified September 2026
policies.summary: USDA established species-specific welfare standards for regulated birds.
policies.changed: Added standards for handling, care, treatment and transport.
policies.afterward: Existing facilities faced August 2023 compliance; new facilities February 2024.
policies.attribution: Biden-era USDA issued the rule; Trump II USDA continues implementation guidance.
policies.unknown: National injury, mortality, compliance and behavioral-welfare changes attributable to the standards.
policies.mechanism: Licensing, registration, inspection and care requirements.
policies.coverage: Birds regulated under the AWA, including covered exhibition, dealing and research contexts.
policies.exceptions: Birds bred for research and agricultural food/fiber uses remain excluded; licensing thresholds apply.
policies.confidenceReason: Rule history and compliance dates verified; outcome estimates were not located in this review.

policies.title: Alaska national-preserve hunting-method rule reversals
policies.status: 2024 baiting restriction; replacement announced October 16, 2026 with delayed effectiveness
policies.summary: Successive NPS rules changed which state-authorized hunting methods are permitted in Alaska preserves.
policies.changed: 2015 restrictions were relaxed in 2020; the 2024 final rule restored the baiting prohibition.
policies.afterward: Interior announced a reversal October 16, 2026, scheduled for October 19 publication and effectiveness 30 days later.
policies.attribution: Agency decisions under four administrations; ANILCA and state/federal authority constrain choices.
policies.unknown: Rule-specific changes in harvest, wounding, suffering or populations; final 2026 text retrieval failed.
policies.mechanism: Restrict or permit hunting methods. Wildlife conservation and individual welfare differ.
policies.coverage: Alaska national preserves; rules must distinguish sport hunting and subsistence.
policies.exceptions: Federal subsistence priority and applicable federal law remain; no nationwide hunting prohibition.
policies.confidenceReason: Prior final rules verified; newest status rests on DOI announcement.

history.event: Final rule prohibited baiting; omitted broader proposed 14-practice table.
DOI announced restoration of state-authorized methods, with delayed effective date.

policies.title: African elephant ivory trade restrictions and later live-import safeguards
policies.status: Commercial restrictions and conditional exceptions described in current FWS guidance
policies.summary: Near-total federal commercial ivory restrictions aimed to reduce U.S. market contributions to elephant decline.
policies.changed: Restricted interstate and foreign ivory commerce; 2024 amendments addressed live-elephant imports and captive care.
policies.afterward: FWS current guidance retains antique/de minimis exceptions and distinguishes possession from commerce.
policies.attribution: Obama-era FWS issued the 2016 rule; Biden-era FWS amended separate live-import/trophy provisions.
policies.unknown: How much U.S. restrictions alone changed poaching, illegal trade or individual suffering.
policies.mechanism: Reduce demand and trade opportunities; conservation pathway with possible welfare consequences.
policies.coverage: African elephant ivory and specified live-elephant transactions.
policies.exceptions: Conditional antiques/de minimis commerce and lawful personal possession; state laws may be stricter.
policies.confidenceReason: Scope verified; no isolated causal effect estimate was located in this review.

cases.caseName: Humane Society of the United States et al. v. National Institutes of Health et al.
cases.court: U.S. District Court for the District of Maryland
cases.disposition: Vacated NIH's Alamogordo transfer-ineligibility decision and remanded; required compliance with statutory sanctuary acceptance.
cases.followup: Chimp Haven reports receiving all remaining Alamogordo chimpanzees in 2025; individual transfer records not audited here.
cases.limitations: Civil judicial review, not animal-cruelty prosecution. No assumption that court alone caused later transfers.

gaps.detail: No complete comparable annual count of all U.S. laboratory animals was verified in this review; APHIS excludes several major populations and NIH's October 2026 expansion remains a proposal.

gaps.impact: No national 'animals saved' estimate or cross-administration causal ranking.

gaps.detail: Roadmaps, awards, draft guidance, future-effective rules and projected savings do not establish realized animal reductions.

gaps.topic: Conflicting NOAA records for 2019 shark-fin imports
gaps.detail: 2020 Atlantic HMS SAFE, published March 2021, Table 8.30, printed p. 211 (PDF p. 234), records preliminary 2019 imports of 1 metric ton total: dried 0, fresh 1, frozen 0 (rw-s-shark-safe2020). The 2024 Shark Finning Report p. 8 states no imports since 2019 (rw-s-shark-report), which may mean after 2019 or reflect revisions. The reason is unverified. The 2019 observation is marked missing/disputed with value null; no source value is silently selected.
gaps.neededData: Reconcile customs product codes, raw trade records, revision history and NOAA explanation of the 2019 boundary year.
gaps.impact: Exclude 2019 from numeric charts and before/after calculations pending reconciliation; retain the documented conflict. The explicit 2023 zero-export observation remains supported.
